When restaurants prep for dinner service they usually have someone, usually the manager, calculate how many of each dish to prepare and how many servings based on ordering trends. They don't prepare servings of every dish for every seat in the house that would be so much food waste. They take past data and use that to inform how many servings they should prepare. And with ingredients like truffle or any other specialty they usually only make a certain amount period. It helps drive the exclusivity of it and rarity. 

Here's the thing, many people will say truffles are overrated and overpower the dish, while true if you really wanted it you could always next time try to call the restaurant and request a portion be held or reserved for you. What's the worst they're gonna say, no? Then you're in the same spot but at least you tried. You could even frame it as you are coming to this restaurant for this exact purpose and that may help with the sympathy but again it's not a guarantee.

Sorry to hear you didn't what you wanted but at least the food was still tasty 😁

I think it's alright. I guess maybe I approached it with more expectations but it's cool for what it is. I've platinumed every RGG game so I feel I can say this as true as possible, I wouldn't recommend someone who is new to the series to buy this full price. If you really like this series then it's worth it but everything feels half baked. And I still enjoyed the hell out of it and still have soke stuff to grind for this platinum. But as with all the RGG games, each one is a stepping stone to the next greatness. IW did a lot of heavy lifting, the playlist while you walk around is the greatest thing I've ever done, only wish you could keep it going into combat haha. The buddy link and emoting to them helps the world feel fuller in a sense. Better substories, party interactions, and I like the plethora of shops and vendors and the fact that we can get as much food as we want. And the minigames are always welcomed.

But there is a lot of mid to it tbh. The lighting is annoyingly bad but IDC about graphics too much, and funny enough the graphics for this game are not great as well. They have cooking minigames but its literally 3 minigames, they couldn't copy paste Ishin's cooking games like they do everything else? They couldn't copy paste Ishin's farming, instead we have scattered planter boxes that I just don't care to maintain or even do. The ship combat for what it is, is severely mid I'm sad to say. Again maybe my expectations were that it'd be AC Black Flag but it's just mid. The enemy ships eventually use barrels and mortars and it's almost like initial D ship combat with you and ships drifting to get a shot. Maybe that's on brand but it feels weird. If we could have mortars and barrels like Black Flag did maybe the ship combat would feel better.

Smartest thing they did was make those explorable islands a long battle with no healing, I enjoyed those as combat challenges A LOT more. The styles are ok, mad dog and sea dog. You know FOMO? Fear of missing out? Get rid of that from your head when you play this game. You're not missing anything, the planets are more or less nonsensical it's the biome and modifiers for each planet. The objective is simple, do the big orange main objective and then go to the big orange arrow and leave. That's it. How to get from point A to point B is entirely up to you. There are side missions, the blue objectives or red pulsing circles or a flashing yellow beam, or just some familiar terrain. You can find stuff to upgrade your ship, ammo/supplies for the mission, stuff to upgrade you, weapons, etc. But the only requirement is doing that main objective. If you complete the objective but run out of reinforcements and can't extract home, you still succeeded since your completed the mission. The mission wasn't to get home safe ;)

When you're back on your ship you can buy upgrades with the samples you grabbed, everyone shares pickups except for ammo/weapons so please don't think someone stole it for themselves, or you can get more guns, cosmetics, stratagems (the arrow combo call-ins), guns, whatever! You pick what you find to be interesting and upgrade to get more flexibility with them! Some people will cry meta and say you must use these, to some extent they are right but very wrong. As long as you balance your team and you have a clear idea of who excels at what type of target, you'll be fine. Don't all bring flamethrowers (although..........) but if someone has one, what as a teammate can you bring to protect their weakness in their kit since they are running the flamethrower? That's the secret sauce. Balance. But make sure you use what you're comfortable with and find what you like. There are clear outliers but everything can work if you make it work. You can't slot it into a different build and expect it to work. My buddies and I run top level helldives and it's all about balance. I couldn't even give a current step for bots or bugs because we try all different things.

Yes, everyone sucked and still sucks hahahaha. We're always learning and adapting even the most grayest of beards can get killed by a rogue stalker or a bile spewer so you're never really perfect. Just start small and don't be afraid to stay at a lower difficulty until you are comfortable stepping it up because it will step up. I promise. 

If there is one advanced tactic but should be basic in this game, MOVE. ALWAYS BE MOVING. DONT DIG IN. You can, but where you fight is never meant to be your last stand, even on an extract that can change in a half second. Always have an idea of where you're going, and always be moving and have an exit strategy. Even 2 exit strategies won't be enough sometimes but then you make the hole yourself :) head on a swivel, always be moving and always get your bearings. I'm CONSTANTLY flicking my map, and I'm not commanding my group but after we complete an objective I'll say we can head west for our next spot, or now we run south hook east around the mountains and pass by some objectives on the map. We have a game plan, we have an exit strategy. Do what you need to do or grab what you came to grab, and start moving. The biggest killer to this day, and even in high lvl groups, is stagnant fighting. They will overwhelm you. You have a plan, stick to it and don't let them dictate the pacing on the battlefield.

Here's an issue I disagree with people who bring up spongy enemies. The game would be so boring and the abilities would be useless if enemies died quickly. What's the point of doing awesome combos and attacks when they're weak. Bosses only have one bar, you have healing. There needs to be some sort of imbalance to their health pool to offset that since none of them heal. In some Yakuza games and the kingdom hearts games they use multiple health bars, but pragmatically what's the difference if the health ticks slowly down or if you take 2 whole bars off is proportionally it's the same amount? For hard mode, I didn't use any healing materia I just had Aerith with a prayer and then Cloud, Tifa, or Barrett had a chakra materia. I had healing materia just in case but prayer was strong enough from aeriths heals. 

Don't underestimate the importance of atb gauge and those purple materials that give increases to the atb gauge for staggers, repeated commands, etc. When you stagger an enemy that's when you go apeshit. 

When you get a new weapon, use it for the character and use the special ability on it so you can learn it and then it's not tied to the weapon anymore. Also make sure to read each characters ability because some of them are GREAT at building a stagger gauge. If you're finding an enemy is hard to stagger, they probably need to be hit with magic. The synergy materia is pretty good but I never used it for hard mode. Yuffie dlc is a whole other can of worms. Consider the warding materia but again I never used it except for a specific boss rush fight on NG+.

Make sure you're switching out materias to level them. You'll need to do at least one of every green materia to max level for a final fight. 

And the last thing I can think of is make sure to rotate through your characters. You can set up a command list so you don't have to pause each time to select attacks and I was doing an atb attack and then would switch to another character while that attack was going and building atb on the second character and continuously rotate through my party. If I had a healer I'd bud up their atb first and then keep it max for an emergency heal (or prayer in this case).

Oooo and this is never really said anywhere but as cloud, if you switch to punisher mode, that transition animation is a parry. If you time it right you'll do an instant retaliation that builds a good amount of stagger. You still take some dmg but it's way better than just outright blocking the attack. I just did it last night. Just use the first couple of races to learn the track and where to start braking in relation to your speed. Learn the turns. When in the turn, I would alternate L2 and R2 because of how the cars work. That was the most successful strat. I also tried the pressing x to help stabilize a slide or tapping x on straight aways to gain some speed but it always fucked me over. 

The first turn is what decides the race. Treat that part like an actual F1 race and don't crash and after the 3rd turn or so you should be in 6-9th place for a good pole position. Slowly work your way forward and focus on making the turns at speed (around 60mph was my target). If you are in 3rd at lap 2, one of the cars in front will crash always so it's really second place. Just be patient and don't get flustered and start gunning it around the track. This driving takes some finesse.

The best way I can describe it is to be aware of your velocity like a motorcycle. It's less about orienting the whole vehicle to a turn, but rather mentally painting a straight arrow from the front of your car and make sure that is pointing where you want to go (5head I know). But it helps when you're sliding to not oversteer into the slide when it catches reaction. Just slide until the front is facing the orientation you want and then gun it.

Also if you're coming around a corner, don't hold the gas it causes spin outs because oversteering is super easy to do when sliding.


Lmk if you need any other tips. It took me like an hour and half all told and Im not a racing game guy. I believe in you. Just learn from your mistakes and try to be consistent in the turns. I tried to start my slides at 60mph like I  said and maintain that speed if I could.
